scope: Bounded complement-mediated aHUS: inherited or acquired complement dysregulation at endothelial surfaces, terminal complement injury and thrombotic microangiopathy. Human cohorts, endothelial assays and animal experiments remain distinct. Excludes STEC-HUS, TTP, secondary TMA, DGKE and cobalamin-related TMA.

paragraphs.text: Eculizumab dose-dependently inhibited activated-serum C5b-9 deposition on glomerular endothelial cultures. C6 or C9 deficiency markedly diminished renal TMA in factor H W1206R mutant mice. C5aR1 removal attenuated clinical disease risk in C3 D1115N mice but renal TMA still developed.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Zymosan may also activate endothelial cells; no clinical efficacy estimate from this experiment. Selected primary-source inspection by an agent; independent domain review pending. Treatment efficacy has not been synthesized in this summary.
